text:
kai: Hey team  excited to be here! First day on an M2 Pro. I cloned the dotfiles and ran the installer but my asdf shims aren't winning: `which node` -> /usr/bin/node, asdf shows nodejs 18.16.0 and python 3.11.4 installed. I also have rustup from a previous dev setup. Using zsh. Any zsh-specific ordering tips? Also what's the usual place for REDWOOD_API_KEY locally for quick experiments (1Password vs direnv vs mac keychain)?
lina: welcome kai :tada: quick wins: 1) put PATH prepends in ~/.zprofile (login shells) not ~/.zshrc. Prepend asdf first: `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"`. 2) add `eval "$(asdf init zsh)"` after PATH. 3) `asdf reshim nodejs` & `asdf reshim python`. If you have rustup, it may add ~/.cargo/bin to PATH — ensure order is correct: asdf shims should come before cargo and /usr/bin.
kai: got it. The installer added asdf lines to ~/.zshrc under an if-block that runs later, so shims were appended too late. Moving them to ~/.zprofile fixed node, but python still points to system python.
lina: did you install the asdf python plugin and set a global? `asdf plugin-add python || true; asdf install python 3.11.4; asdf global python 3.11.4; asdf reshim python`. Also macOS sometimes ships a /usr/bin/python3; run `hash -r` or open a new login shell to clear zsh cache.
kai: installed plugin and global, reshim worked  python now OK. One oddity: when I open a new GUI terminal window it doesn't source ~/.zprofile so VSCode integrated terminal still sees system node. Thoughts?
lina: VSCode sometimes launches non-login shells. In Settings set terminal.integrated.shellArgs.osx to ["-l"] so it runs as login shell, or move necessary PATH exports to ~/.zshenv (careful: that runs for every shell including non-interactive). Another approach: ensure direnv is loaded and add a small .envrc that exports PATH for the project.
kai: speaking of direnv, where do people store REDWOOD_API_KEY? 1Password entry name isn't obvious in my vault.
infra: we keep service and personal dev tokens in 1Password. Personal dev keys are named `redwood-temp-<firstname>` (short-lived). For local usage we prefer direnv: add `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` to a local .envrc and `direnv allow`. Don't commit to dotfiles. For long-lived CI tokens open an infra ticket.
kai: thanks. I also saw my dotfiles try to symlink a launch agent for ssh-agent which apparently fails under Fast User Switching on macOS  ssh keys aren't autoloading. Any workaround?
lina: common pattern: add `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` to your login script and ensure `UseKeychain yes` in ~/.ssh/config. If the launch agent is flaky, the fallback in dotfiles is `scripts/ssh-load.sh` which runs at interactive shell startup and tolerates fast-user scenarios.
kai: last snag: GPG commit signing import fails with pinentry-curses error. Installed pinentry-mac but gpg still pops up an odd GUI prompt.
lina: try `brew install pinentry-mac` then add `pinentry-program /opt/homebrew/bin/pinentry-mac` to ~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf and `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` in ~/.zprofile. Then `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent && gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`. If still GUI weirdness, check your GPG suite prefs; sometimes macOS keychain interop causes prompts.
tonY: (ops) small infra note: if you need a scoped test API key for experimenting with the hosted API, open a short ticket in #support and we'll create `redwood-temp-<name>-dev` limited to non-prod endpoints. Also: never store production keys in dotfiles or plain Git.
devex-bot: (bot) Hi kai  If you'd like a 30m setup pairing we can do a screenshare. Reply "pair" here and I'll DM available slots. Handbooks: https://handbook.redwood.dev/onboarding/dev-setup and script `dotfiles/scripts/migrate-brew.sh` for handling mixed /usr/local vs /opt/homebrew setups.
kai: great, moving my asdf init to ~/.zprofile and adding the gpg fixes. I'll ping if anything else pops up and may take that pairing. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:"
